results.references: - Alexander Tyurin. [Optimality in Decentralized Optimization under Bandwidth Constraints](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.20735v1). 2026 (preprint v1, 21 March). Complexity: $O\!\left(\frac{L\Delta}{\varepsilon}\min_{1\le k\le n}\min_{1\le p\le k}\min_{1\le m\le |S_{k,p}|}\left[\frac{d}{\bar w_k}+\frac{m+\sigma^2/\varepsilon}{\sum_{i=1}^{m}h_{\pi_i(S_{k,p})}^{-1}}\right]\right)$ elapsed time for Grace SGD to obtain $\mathbb E\|\nabla f(\bar x)\|^2\le\varepsilon$, for $0<\varepsilon\le L\Delta$. Here $\bar w_k$ are sorted Gomory–Hu tree weights, $\bar w_n=\infty$, $S_{k,p}$ are components after deleting the first $k-1$ tree edges, and $\pi(S)$ sorts workers by increasing $h_i$. The communication analysis measures bandwidth in real coordinates per unit time; local preprocessing and arithmetic have negligible cost.

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained minimization of a differentiable function f on R^d. The gradient is globally L-Lipschitz, and some global lower bound a satisfies f(x₀)−a≤Δ. Convexity is not required. Parameters satisfy L>0, Δ≥0, σ≥0, and ε>0.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: All workers access the same jointly measurable stochastic gradient g(x,ξ), with E[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x) and E‖g(x,ξ)−∇f(x)‖²≤σ². Samples are IID within each worker and independent across workers, with common marginal μ. A query (x,m) returns m gradients and occupies worker i for m h_i time; each worker permits one pending computation.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GraphBandwidthSmoothNonconvex.lean: system and spec.admissible; LongTails/Setups/BandwidthHeterogeneousSmoothNonconvex.lean: ComputeQuery and computation; LongTails/Setups/StochasticSmoothAndConvex.lean: IsStochasticGradient; LongTails/Setups/StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.lean: IID.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: The unbiased gradient noise has uniformly bounded second central moment σ². No almost-sure noise bound, exponential-tail assumption, or sample-gradient smoothness is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is EuclideanSpace R (Fin d), with d any natural number and the Euclidean norm.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Elapsed-time distributed model with n≥1 workers, positive heterogeneous gradient times h_i, and a connected graph with positive symmetric edge bandwidths b_ij. A directed link serializes finite-bit messages, taking message length divided by b_ij, with no additional latency. Different links and workers can operate concurrently. Every transmitted message receives a 64-bit clock overhead. Allowed algorithms realize fixed-batch minibatch SGD with local and aggregate clipping and quantization, and a uniformly selected iterate. All Params are public, including G, b, h, L, Δ, σ, ε, and x₀; f, g, and the sampling laws are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/GraphBandwidthSmoothNonconvex.lean: communication, SgdTuning, SgdTuning.quantize, SgdTuning.iterate, IsQuantizedMinibatchSgd, and spec; LongTails/TemplateDistributed.lean: clockBits, step, and TimedConvergence.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm_squared
accuracy.details: The measurable output must have integrable squared gradient norm and satisfy E‖∇f(output)‖²≤ε. The criterion uses ε directly, not ε². The allowed algorithm terminates with X_J at its root, where J is uniform on {0,…,K−1}.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The stationarity guarantee is in expectation over algorithm randomization and oracle samples under their product law, at the supplied fixed elapsed-time budget. TimedConvergence additionally requires almost-sure finiteness of execution events through that deadline.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The smooth nonconvex stochastic objective and expected stationarity criterion are standard, but the setup additionally specifies heterogeneous computation times, queued per-bit graph communication, clock overhead, and a restricted quantized minibatch algorithm class under an elapsed-time budget.
